Mixed Model of the Integrated Brier Score on Alpha and Lambda

Source: R/tune_diagnostics_grid.R
tbl_tune_mixed_model.Rd

Fits `IBS ~ alpha * log10(lambda) + (1 | resample)` to a tuning grid with [lme4::lmer()] and returns the fixed effects as a table, so the report does not have to rebuild the model and its `gtsummary` call in every chapter.

Usage

tbl_tune_mixed_model(
  data,
  log_ibs = FALSE,
  random = NULL,
  interaction = TRUE,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  format = c("tibble", "gtsummary")
)

Arguments

data

A tuning table with `alpha`, `lambda`, `IBS` and a resample column (`inner_resamples_splits`, `inner_resamples` or `split`). Rows are reduced to one per model.

log_ibs

If `TRUE`, the response is `log10(IBS)`. Default `FALSE`.

random

Optional names of further grouping columns that get a random intercept each (for example the outer fold), in addition to the resample column.

interaction

If `TRUE` (default) the model has the `alpha` by `log10(lambda)` interaction.

conf_level

Confidence level (default 0.95).

format

`"tibble"` (default) or `"gtsummary"`, a [gtsummary::tbl_regression()] table (needs the broom.helpers package, and broom.mixed for a mixed model).

Value

A tibble with `term`, `estimate`, `std.error`, `statistic`, `conf.low`, `conf.high` and `p.value`, with the fitted model in `attr(, "model")`, the formula in `attr(, "formula")` and `attr(, "method")` (`"lmer"` or `"lm"`); or a `gtsummary` table.

Inference

The tibble reports Wald intervals and p-values from the normal approximation (`estimate / std.error`) for the mixed model, which is reasonable here because a tuning grid has many models per resample; they are optimistic when there are few resamples. The models of one grid are fitted to the same data, so treat the p-values as a description of the response surface, not as tests. When there is a single resample, lme4 is not installed, or the mixed model fails, an ordinary linear model is fitted instead and `attr(, "method")` is `"lm"`; for that fallback the intervals and p-values use the t-distribution with the model's residual degrees of freedom, which is the correct small-sample reference distribution for `lm`.

See also

[fit_ibs_mixed_model()], [tbl_tune_alpha()], [plot_tune_grid()]

Examples

set.seed(1)
tune <- expand.grid(split = paste0("Fold", 1:4), alpha = c(0.1, 0.5, 1),
                    lambda = c(0.01, 0.05, 0.1))
tune$IBS <- 0.15 + 0.03 * tune$alpha + 0.1 * tune$lambda + stats::rnorm(nrow(tune), 0, 0.01)
tbl_tune_mixed_model(tune)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 7
#>   term               estimate std.error statistic conf.low conf.high  p.value
#>   <chr>                 <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 (Intercept)         0.166     0.00974    17.0    0.147      0.185  3.54e-65
#> 2 alpha               0.0237    0.0150      1.58  -0.00571    0.0532 1.14e- 1
#> 3 log10_lambda        0.00793   0.00652     1.22  -0.00485    0.0207 2.24e- 1
#> 4 alpha:log10_lambda -0.00605   0.0101     -0.601 -0.0258     0.0137 5.48e- 1
